solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Laden with frock, twirling Morris fan?

indicators.note: twirling spins things round, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer spins in a heavily laden frock, perhaps a devotee of morris dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling' rearranges LADEN FROCK. 'Morris' is morris dancing, a traditional English folk dance with bells and sticks; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen follower of morris, the English traditional dance, is an example of someone who performs country dances.

clue.text: Maroon thread

definitions.meaning: to maroon someone is to leave them stuck on a shore, beached
a single fibre or filament of yarn

explanation.surface: A dark reddish-brown thread for sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to leave someone stuck ashore, and a single filament of yarn or hair.

clue.text: Lousy writer yet singular swimmer

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
someone doing the front crawl stroke is a crawler

explanation.surface: A poor author who is also, oddly, a lone swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scribbles illegibly or carelessly is a bad writer of handwriting or prose.

clue.text: Ran off, following light

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small lamp

explanation.surface: Someone bolted, chasing a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: to run off from danger is to have escaped or bolted.

clue.text: Dig into old film company for dress coat

parts.note: to claw is to dig into with nails or talons
Hammer Films was the British studio famed for horror movies

explanation.surface: An old movie studio rummages for a formal coat for a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Hammer was a British studio known for 1950s-70s horror films.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailcoat whose split tails resemble the forked end of that tool was called by this name.

clue.text: Britain upset farmers over government defence system

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the abbreviation for Britain upside down

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom

indicators.note: here over means covering, so the farmers' letters sit round the next piece

parts.note: the NFU is Britain's National Farmers' Union

explanation.surface: British farmers revolt against the government's defence policy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means sitting on top of, here wrapping round the government piece; the farmers are Britain's National Farmers' Union.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese martial art is a system of unarmed combat used for self-protection.

clue.text: Towering performance by old clown

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
antic is an archaic word for a grotesque performer or buffoon

explanation.surface: A tall-standing act put on by a veteran clown.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTIC as a noun once meant a clown, as in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something towering is enormous in size, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Joint's been known to go belly- up, ignoring margins

indicators.note: to go belly-up is to turn over, so in a down entry the letters are read upwards
ignoring the edges of the phrase leaves a run of letters from its inside

explanation.surface: A joint has been known to fail completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring margins' takes EENK from the inside of 'been known'; 'go belly- up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Fancy political hero harbouring American misperception!

indicators.note: fancy as a verb is to imagine, so the letters of political are reworked
harbouring means holding inside, so the hero's letters surround the next piece

parts.note: a lion is a brave or celebrated person, a hero
US, short for United States

explanation.surface: An elaborate political hero who shelters an American turns out to be a delusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective on the politician but signals the rearrangement; a 'lion' is a celebrated or brave figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual trick that deceives the eye is a kind of false perception.

clue.text: Floor in the style of Oz native

parts.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, KO in boxing
a la, from French, means in the manner or style of

explanation.surface: Flooring laid in the manner of something native to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: This marsupial is native to Australia, which is nicknamed Oz.

clue.text: Lower feathers got darker, so some picked up

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathering of birds

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so some listeners hear the past tense of turning grey

parts.note: greyed means became greyer, darkened

explanation.surface: Feathers that grew darker and were collected by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower something's rank or status is to reduce its level.

clue.text: Part of Spain joined with States, inter alia

parts.note: and joins one thing with another

indicators.note: inter is Latin for between or among, so the states go among the letters of alia

parts.note: US, the United States

explanation.surface: A region of Spain linked to America, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase 'inter alia' (among other things) is split: 'inter' means between, acting on 'alia'.
explanation.definitionFit: This autonomous region in the south of the Iberian kingdom includes Seville and Granada.

clue.text: Alfred's mad hiding, say, rare trait of narcissus

indicators.note: hiding means keeping something inside, so the jumbled name surrounds the next pieces
mad means crazy, so the letters of the name are scrambled

parts.note: eg, for example, signals an instance

explanation.surface: Mad Alfred concealing a rare example of vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: R for rare is a dictionary abbreviation; the scrambled name splits around the hidden pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus, the youth in Greek myth who fell for his own reflection, typifies excessive vanity and self-love.

clue.text: Extremist caught in Istanbul trap

indicators.note: caught in signals the letters held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A radical is snared in a trap in Istanbul.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding extreme views, such as a die-hard royalist or fanatic, is called by this word.

clue.text: Wipe out Athenian rebels, saving the Italian

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so the jumbled letters hold the next piece
to rebel is to revolt, so the letters of the Greek word rise up into a new order

parts.note: il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Greek rebels destroy everyone except one Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' reads as a noun for the surface but works as a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy completely or exterminate is to eliminate utterly.

clue.text: Person from Panama or Rhode Island?

definitions.meaning: someone from the isthmus nation between Colombia and Costa Rica
Rhode Island is abbreviated RI, the two middle letters of the nationality word

explanation.surface: Is this person from Panama or from Rhode Island?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: RI (Rhode Island) is the centre of AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama lies on the isthmus linking the two continents of the New World, so its people are from that region.

clue.text: Call left good Parisian looking up count maybe

indicators.note: in a down entry looking up means the pieces are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to call is to name
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A call left a good Parisian looking up to a count.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is one example of a titled aristocrat, alongside dukes and earls.

clue.text: Nymph in grass bounced back again

indicators.note: in places the nymph inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall water grass
Echo was the nymph of Greek myth who could only repeat others

explanation.surface: A nymph in the grass sprang back again.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that rebounds a second time has resounded once more.

clue.text: Puzzle on coach for Edinburgh cop

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A puzzle set on a coach for a Scottish detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Edinburgh cop' is a second definition: John Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture riddle in which images or letters stand for words is this kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Tried to locate son with nothing except number

parts.note: S for son, as in genealogies

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so the number abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: nought means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Someone searched for a son with nothing but a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of seek: to have looked for something is to have searched.

clue.text: Element of Blue Planet?

parts.note: a blue steak is extremely underdone, rare
the earth is our planet

explanation.surface: Part of the Blue Planet, Earth's nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like colour but is the steak sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanide metals such as cerium and neodymium are each one of this group of elements.

clue.text: Let slip show, touching flesh

parts.note: re means touching, concerning
veal is calf's flesh, meat

explanation.surface: Someone lets slip a show of touching flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' is a second definition alongside 'Let slip'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose a secret inadvertently is to divulge it.

clue.text: Dredge up rocks about 1st of July? It's decided beforehand

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shaken letters go round the next piece
to rock is to shake, so the letters of the phrase are shaken up
1st of selects the first letter of the month

explanation.surface: Dredging up rocks around the start of July was settled in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' rearranges DREDGEUP; 'about' puts J around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessed before the evidence was in: a judgement formed in advance.

clue.text: Roughly handle new puppet

parts.note: to paw is to handle clumsily or roughly

explanation.surface: Someone manhandles a new marionette.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used by others as a tool, like a chess piece moved at will.

clue.text: Cross over entrance

indicators.note: over means turned over, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix or cross, as in a church rood screen

explanation.surface: Walk across, over the threshold.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel closing a way in is how one enters a building or room.

clue.text: Husband nearly finished large hole

indicators.note: nearly means almost all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: over means finished
L for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A husband has nearly finished digging a big hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole is slang for a squalid, wretched dwelling, a hut unfit to live in.

clue.text: Stand for European pitch met estimate

parts.note: to weather a storm is to stand or endure it
to pitch is to throw, cast

explanation.surface: A European stands for a pitch where a meeting was estimated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'met' is the Met Office, Britain's national weather service.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorologist's prediction of tomorrow's conditions is this kind of outlook.
